app_note: PayNest is a FICTIONAL payments app invented for this academic project. It is not affiliated with any real company.
support_line: Open PayNest, go to Profile > Help & Support, and use the in-app support chat. Do not use phone numbers or links that someone sent you.

example_queries: someone called saying my kyc is expiring
my kyc will be blocked unless I update now
message says verify kyc or account will be suspended
caller says I must update my pan and aadhaar details immediately
kyc verification link received on whatsapp
they said my wallet will be closed today if I do not complete kyc
red_flags: Urgency or a deadline
Threat of blocking or closing your account
Asks for OTP, PIN or card details
Sends a link or asks you to install an app
entries.answer: This looks like a fake KYC scam. PayNest will never call or message you demanding urgent KYC, and will never ask for your OTP, PIN or password. Do not click any link, install any app or share any code. End the call. If you are worried about your KYC status, open the PayNest app yourself and check it there, or contact support through the in-app Help & Support chat.

example_queries: I got a link to claim my refund
someone sent a refund link for my failed transaction
message says click here to receive cashback
they asked me to open a link to get my money back
refund link asks me to enter my card details
reward message with a link to claim it
red_flags: Refund you were not expecting
Link from an unknown number or shortened URL
Page asks for card number, PIN or OTP
Pressure to act quickly
entries.answer: Treat this as a phishing attempt. Genuine refunds are credited automatically to your original payment method and never need you to click a link or enter your PIN or OTP. Do not open the link or enter any details. Check your refund status inside the PayNest app under Transaction History, or ask in-app support.

entries.category: Send Rs 1 to receive money trick
example_queries: buyer says send rs 1 to receive money
they asked me to pay 1 rupee to get the payment
I got a request to send a small amount to receive my money
stranger said approve a collect request to receive payment
to receive money you need to enter your pin they said
buyer wants me to send a test payment of 1 rupee first
red_flags: You are asked to pay or enter a PIN in order to receive money
A collect or request notification you did not expect
Buyer insists on a small test payment
entries.answer: This is a known trick. You never need to enter your PIN, approve a request or send any amount in order to receive money. Entering your PIN always sends money out. Decline the request, do not send anything, and block the sender. If you already approved a payment, open in-app support right away.

entries.category: OTP or PIN requested by someone
example_queries: support asked for my otp
should I share otp for kyc
caller says they are from paynest and needs my otp
someone asked me for my upi pin to fix my account
agent wants the code that came on my phone
is it ok to tell my otp to the customer care person
red_flags: Anyone asking for OTP, PIN, password or CVV
A caller claiming to be support
Request to read out or forward a code
entries.answer: Never share your OTP, PIN, password or CVV with anyone, including people who say they are from PayNest. Real support never asks for these. End the call or chat. If you already shared a code, immediately open the app, change your PIN and contact in-app support.

entries.category: I clicked a suspicious link or entered details
example_queries: I clicked a suspicious link
I entered my card details on a fake page
I already shared my otp what do I do
I installed an app that a caller told me to install
I opened a refund link and typed my pin
I think I gave my details to a scammer
entries.answer: Act quickly. 1) Change your PayNest PIN and password from inside the app. 2) If you installed an app at someone's request, uninstall it and turn on airplane mode until you have removed it. 3) Contact your bank or card provider if card details were entered. 4) Report the incident through in-app Help & Support so the account can be reviewed. 5) Keep screenshots of messages and the sender's details. Do not delay, since speed matters.

example_queries: money was deducted without my permission
I see a transaction I did not make
unknown payment shows in my history
someone took money from my account
unauthorised debit from my wallet
my balance dropped and I did not pay anyone
entries.answer: Open the PayNest app and review Transaction History to confirm it is not a payment you forgot. If it really is unauthorised, change your PIN and password now, then report the transaction through in-app Help & Support with the date, amount and reference number. Also tell your bank if your linked bank account was involved.

example_queries: I found a customer care number online
someone claiming to be paynest support called me
support agent asked me to install screen sharing app
a helpline number from a search result asked for my details
they asked me to share my screen to fix my account
is this support number real
red_flags: Number found in search results or social media
Asks you to install remote access or screen sharing
Calls you first without you raising a complaint
entries.answer: Only use the support channel inside the PayNest app (Profile > Help & Support). Numbers from search results, social media or unexpected callers can be fake. Real support will never ask you to share your screen, install remote-access apps or read out codes. If you have already done so, uninstall the app and change your PIN.

entries.category: Fake buyer or QR code scam
example_queries: buyer sent a qr code and asked me to scan it to receive money
someone wants to buy my item and asked me to scan a code
marketplace buyer says scan this to get paid
advance payment buyer wants my pin
I am selling something and the buyer sent a payment request
scan this qr to get your money they said
red_flags: Scanning a QR code to receive money
Buyer sends requests instead of paying directly
Buyer rushes you or avoids meeting
entries.answer: Scanning a QR code or entering a PIN only ever sends money out. You do not need to do either to receive a payment. Do not scan the code. Ask the buyer to pay you directly using your own payment ID, and confirm the money actually shows in your Transaction History before handing over anything.

example_queries: I got a message saying I won a lottery
they said I won a prize and need to pay a processing fee
congratulations message asks for my bank details to send gift
lucky draw winner message with a link
free gift but I must pay a delivery charge first
message says I have reward points that expire today
red_flags: Prize for a contest you never entered
Fee required to receive the prize
Request for bank or card details
entries.answer: This is a prize scam. You cannot win a contest you did not enter, and real prizes never require you to pay a fee or share your PIN or OTP first. Ignore the message, do not click links, and block the sender. Report the message through in-app support if it uses PayNest's name.

example_queries: part time job offer on telegram paying per task
they promise guaranteed returns if I invest
work from home job asks me to pay a registration fee
someone offered to double my money
I was added to a group that shares investment tips and asks me to transfer money
task job where I first deposit money then get commission
red_flags: Guaranteed or very high returns
Pay first, earn later
Contact through messaging apps from strangers
entries.answer: Be careful. Guaranteed returns, pay-first jobs and tasks that need a deposit are classic scam patterns. Do not transfer money to people you only know online. If you already paid, stop paying more, keep screenshots and report it through in-app support.

fallback_answer: I am not sure this matches a scam I know about, so I will not guess. As a safe rule: never share your OTP, PIN or password with anyone, and do not click links from unknown senders. For help with this specific situation, please use the in-app Help & Support chat (Profile > Help & Support).
off_topic_answer: I can only help with spotting and responding to digital payment scams for PayNest users. Try describing a suspicious call, message, link or transaction.
refusal_answer: I cannot help with that. I can explain how to protect your own account or how to recognise scams if that is useful.
injection_answer: I cannot change my rules or share my instructions. I can still help you check whether a call, message or link looks like a scam.
sensitive_input_warning: It looks like your message contains a code, PIN, password or card number. Please do not share these with anyone, including me. I have removed it from what I process. If you already shared it with someone, change your PIN in the app now and contact in-app support.
